subject: ObsidianHealth activation ask — sprint bump for tenant telemetry & residency
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ObsidianHealth activation ask — sprint bump for tenant telemetry & residency

Team,

Quick background: ObsidianHealth (large healthcare SaaS) is at legal/procurement and has sign-off conditions tied to two features before they will execute the committed annual contract: (1) per-tenant encrypted telemetry export that can be routed to their customer-managed S3 (they need a separate stream for audit purposes), and (2) a residency guarantee for a small set of model sessions for their highest-volume customers (session affinity + soft pinning to a Dedicated pool for the first 30 minutes).

They are asking if we can move these items into the next engineering sprint (starting in 7 calendar days) so their procurement can hit the vendor onboarding date. The commercial ask: $600k ACV on signature this quarter. If we miss the procurement milestone they will delay signing for another quarter.

Attachments: obsidian_deal_outline.pdf (procurement timeline + contract excerpt).

What I need from product/eng: a short feasibility note (can we ship a safe, limited-scope implementation of both items in one sprint?), a clear list of risks, and an MVP acceptance criteria we can share with Obsidian. If a full implementation is not feasible in sprint-1, please propose a phased approach we can commit to (dates + deliverables).

Laura: can you confirm CS/regulatory asks on the telemetry side (retention/window/encryption) so we don't miss requirements.

Thanks — I think this is a deal we should bend for if the risk is contained.

Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 12:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: ObsidianHealth activation ask — sprint bump for tenant telemetry & residency

Sean —

Thanks for the context and the attachment. High-level thoughts: both asks are reasonable but non-trivial from a product-safety and observability perspective. I want to avoid rushed implementations that introduce audit/PII risk or cause a platform outage.

A few clarifying questions before I commit to a sprint bump:
- Telemetry export: do they require real-time streaming (sub-1min delivery) or is a nearline export (5-15 min window) acceptable? Also, what retention and encryption controls are mandated (server-side encryption with CMK, retention 7/30/90 days)?
- Residency: is the ask hard pinning (guaranteed residency on a particular Dedicated host) or soft affinity (preferential warm routing + session priority)? Hard pinning has large operational cost.
- Success criteria: please propose the concrete acceptance criteria the customer will sign off on (latency, delivery window, audit fields present).

Ben — can you sketch feasibility and an estimate in story points? If this is 2+ sprints we should propose a phased delivery: phase 1 = nearline telemetry export + session-priority routing; phase 2 = customer-managed delivery endpoints + stronger residency guarantees.

I can coordinate priority inside product if we get a short tech note from eng.

—Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: ObsidianHealth activation ask — sprint bump for tenant telemetry & residency

Marissa / Sean —

Technical gut check and quick estimate: both features are implementable but there are caveats. Short version: we can deliver a limited-scope Phase 1 inside one engineering sprint (2 weeks) with a focused scope and a runtime guardrail. Details below.

Telemetry export (Phase 1): nearline export (approximately 5-10 minute batching) to a customer-provided S3 bucket with server-side encryption enforced (we can support SSE-KMS). We'll include a minimal audit schema (request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, route, model_id, token_counts). Caveat: not all internal derived signals will be exportable in sprint-1 (e.g., full token-level provenance). Risk: improper schema could force a backwards-incompatible change later. Effort: ~6 story points.

Residency (Phase 1): session-priority shim that marks sessions from Obsidian as high-priority and routes them to a pre-warmed Dedicated lane for the first 30 minutes. This is a routing + scheduling change, not hard pinning. True hard pinning (binding to a single host) requires infra and billing plumbing and is 3+ sprints. Effort: ~8 story points. Risks: warm pool sizing, burst amplification if they scale beyond predicted traffic. Mitigation: we can gate the feature behind a toggle and apply a traffic cap per tenant.

Estimate summary: 14 story points total. If we allocate this into the next sprint we can deliver Phase 1 (nearline telemetry + session-priority routing) with toggleable rollout, acceptance tests, and a short-runbook for SRE. Production readiness (phase 2 features like streaming, stronger residency guarantees, CMK key proofs) is another 2-3 sprints.

I'll attach a sketch of the temporary-shim-design.png with the proposed routing flags and telemetry export flow. We must also prioritize a short privacy/data checklist with Legal/Trust — Laura can you own that?

Ben
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@obsidianhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 15:08:30 -0700
Subject: Re: ObsidianHealth activation ask — sprint bump for tenant telemetry & residency

Maya — looping you in with our proposed path. Internal summary below and ask for a quick confirmation from your side so we can lock sprint planning tomorrow AM.

Proposed Phase 1 (one sprint deliverable):
- Nearline telemetry export (5-10 minute batch) to Obsidian-managed S3 with SSE-KMS. Schema: request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, route, model_id, token_counts.
- Session-priority routing: sessions flagged as "obsidian_high" will be routed to a pre-warmed Dedicated lane for the first 30 minutes; soft affinity only, capped at X concurrent sessions (we will share a burst cap).

Acceptance criteria for Phase 1 (what we need you to confirm):
1) Nearline window of 10 minutes is acceptable for your audit needs.
2) SSE-KMS on your S3 is fine and we can validate via a test object.
3) You accept soft residency (no absolute host pinning) with a concurrency cap of 150 sessions for initial rollout.

If you confirm the three points above, we will schedule the work in the next sprint (kickoff in 48 hours) and provide a delivery ETA (expected deploy to staging by EOD sprint+10 days). Phase 2 (streaming + hard pinning) is dependent on further infra work and a separate timeline.

Maya — can you reply with confirmation or which items need to change? Procurement is waiting for our committed milestone to finalize signatures.

Thanks,
Sean
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@obsidianhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Li <aaron.li@obsidianhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ObsidianHealth activation ask — sprint bump for tenant telemetry & residency

Sean / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the clear plan. We can accept Phase 1 with the conditions below:
- 10 minute nearline export is acceptable for initial onboarding provided the exported schema includes request_id, tenant_id, timestamp, and model_id.
- SSE-KMS to our S3 is fine; procurement will request a short technical attestation that the objects are encrypted with our CMK.
- Soft residency is acceptable for the first release but we need a firm date for Phase 2 commitments (streaming + stronger residency) because our rollout to customers is timed to that capability. Procurement is targeting a signed PO by 2028-06-10; if you can confirm sprint allocation and a projected Phase 2 kickoff date by 2028-06-05 we can proceed to signature.

We also need a short runbook entry describing failure modes (what happens if the warm pool is exceeded and we failover).

If you can provide those points by COB Monday we will proceed.

Maya Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships
ObsidianHealth
